newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean soldier surrenders after taking hostage.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean soldier surrenders after taking hostage.

text.p: A South Korean soldier, who had held a woman hostage for about three hours in a travel agency in the east coast city of Kangnung, surrendered to police on Wednesday, a police official said.
"He surrendered after his elder brother, his girlfriend and his senior sergeant together persuaded him," the official said by telephone from the east coast city.
He said only a woman had been taken hostage, correcting an earlier report by the state Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) that three people had been taken hostage.
The soldier, marine private Chung Chi-hi, entered the travel agency after escaping from military police who were trying to arrest him on a charge of desertion, the official said.
Chung, who deserted from barracks on Sunday, was carrying no military arms but a knife, the police official said.
Kangnung is about 170 km (106 miles) east of the capital Seoul.
